claims.statement: The concept has FPT/GHEC/GHES metadata and historical redirects; individual conditional sections and feature files narrow applicability.

Hardcoded cloud secrets require creating and duplicating cloud credentials. With a provider supporting OIDC and an established trust relationship, a workflow can instead request a short-lived cloud access token.
OIDC can remove the need to duplicate long-lived cloud credentials in repository secrets by configuring cloud trust and updating the workflow; it does not eliminate all secrets automatically.
Cloud authentication and authorization controls can constrain workflow access to cloud resources. A token alone does not prove those constraints were configured.
The source describes provider-issued job-limited expiring credentials; this is a claim about the documented OIDC model, not a measured lifetime of a live provider token.

The diagram and prose describe cloud trust for specified workflows/role, a GitHub job identity JWT, and a cloud-issued access token after validation. Neither depiction proves a target validates claims or executes a job.

The provider compares the JWT subject and other claims with conditions configured on the cloud role. Access is conditional on the configured claims matching; this description is not a live trust-policy verification.

The JWT is an example with placeholder identifiers, GHES-versus-dotcom issuer/audience substitution and separately gated enterprise/custom-property fields. Do not copy it as deployed trust or a universal subject format.

The example uses an older subject format. New repositories after July 15, 2026 use default immutable owner/repository IDs; this default is unavailable on GHES. Old name-only examples are not universal current defaults.
Inside the GHEC section, trust must permit only authorized workflows; the provider matches the subject and configured conditions before issuing temporary access. Retain the section condition.

Inside the GHEC section and Dependabot-OIDC feature condition, Dependabot update jobs use event_name dynamic. An Actions-only trust policy should allow expected workflow event names when the provider supports that condition. Do not apply this nested passage to all products.

Enterprises using Cloud data residency on GHE.com must substitute certain OIDC configuration values. The linked reference specifies the substitutions; this concept does not supply a complete target configuration.
Custom actions can request an OIDC token through toolkit getIDToken or curl. This description alone does not verify requesting permissions, job execution or issuance.
Provider login actions can simplify updating workflows from secrets to OIDC; linked provider-specific setup remains follow-up evidence, not completed configuration.

For the FPT/GHEC custom-property feature, admins define and assign repository properties, select claims for inclusion, then update cloud trust conditions. Enabled values appear with repo_property_ prefixes without workflow-level changes.

Within the FPT/GHEC-only custom-property feature, custom properties must already exist at organization/enterprise level, and configuration requires an organization or enterprise admin. A repository user is not automatically authorized.

Within the FPT/GHEC-only custom-property feature, the article offers UI or the organization OIDC customization API to include property claims. This reference is not permission to mutate organization settings or a verified request schema.

Within the FPT/GHEC-only custom-property feature, the custom-property JWT is illustrative and uses a name-based sub alongside property claims; it does not override the immutable-default caveat or certify property limits.

Where the Dependabot-OIDC feature applies (FPT/GHEC; GHES later than 3.20), private registries using username/password can use OIDC on AWS CodeArtifact, Azure DevOps Artifacts or JFrog Artifactory. Do not generalize this to every registry.

Within the Dependabot OIDC feature available for FPT/GHEC and GHES newer than 3.20, the article lists reduced static credentials, simpler management and avoidance of static-token rate limits as benefits. These are not measurements of a particular rollout.
Deployment and OIDC-reference links remain unreviewed follow-ups outside this concept batch.

scope: Pinned full-article reading with literal includes, selected variables and visual dependencies; source claims only, no adoption or live behavior assertion.
